findings.title: Unclear Main Menu Contrast
findings.where: Title screen: 'SMDUEL' text, tagline, and menu options.
findings.problem: The main game title, tagline, and interactive menu options (New Driver, Controls) have low contrast against the background image. The 'Arcade' button also suffers from this.
findings.why: This makes key navigational elements and the game's identity difficult to read quickly, especially for players with visual impairments or on screens with poor calibration. It feels unfinished and lacks impact.
findings.fix: Apply a stronger, consistent color with better luminosity contrast to all text elements, or add a subtle text shadow/outline to improve readability without obscuring the background entirely. The 'Arcade' button needs a more distinct background color or border.

findings.title: Minimalist Radar Functionality
findings.where: All gameplay screens (Arena, Road, City): bottom-left radar display.
findings.problem: The radar is a static green circle with no visible sweep animation, contacts, or discernible directional indication beyond 'orientations: north-up'. It looks like a placeholder.
findings.why: A radar without an active sweep or visible targets provides no immediate feedback or utility. Players can't quickly discern threats, objectives, or their own orientation in a dynamic environment, making it feel broken or non-functional rather than an instrument.
findings.fix: Implement a clear radar sweep animation (e.g., a rotating line), add distinct visual cues for targets/points of interest (e.g., dots, icons), and consider adding a visual representation of the player's current facing direction on the radar itself.

findings.title: UI Element Clutter on City Screen
findings.where: City screen: top-right condition/info panel and bottom-right 'Fight | Build | Care | Jobs' panel.
findings.problem: The condition panel (seen in other screens) is unnecessarily present and largely empty/irrelevant on the city screen, covering a significant portion of the top-right gameplay area. The bottom-right actions are also very small and blend into the background.
findings.why: Irrelevant information clutters the screen and distracts from the core gameplay loop (navigation and interaction within the city). The tiny action buttons are hard to notice and interact with, hindering player agency and feeling like an afterthought.
findings.fix: Remove or collapse the condition panel when in the city view. Enlarge and reposition the 'Fight | Build | Care | Jobs' buttons, giving them more visual weight, clearer iconography, and better contrast so they are immediately identifiable as interactive elements.

findings.title: Inconsistent Player Car Visual Hierarchy
findings.where: All gameplay screens (Arena, Road, City): the player's car.
findings.problem: The player's car model, while visible, blends significantly into the background tiles/textures due to similar color palettes and lack of a strong visual differentiator (e.g., outline, glow, distinct shading).
findings.why: The player's own vehicle is the primary point of focus. If it blends in, it makes it harder to track quickly, especially during combat or fast-paced movement, leading to eyestrain or a feeling of disconnect from the avatar.
findings.fix: Apply a subtle but distinct outline to the player's car, or adjust its material/lighting to make it pop more against the ground. Consider a slight emissive glow or a higher contrast color for key parts of the car. This ensures it is always the most prominent object.

findings.title: Monochromatic Vehicle Constructor UI
findings.where: Vehicle Constructor screen: entire left panel (part list) and right panel (stats, schematic).
findings.problem: The entire UI in the vehicle constructor is predominantly shades of teal/dark grey, lacking visual differentiation between interactive elements, selected items, and static information. The schematic is also very flat.
findings.why: A monochromatic UI makes it hard to distinguish between selectable options, currently active selections, and static data. This can lead to confusion, slow down decision-making, and make the experience feel dull and unengaging. The flat schematic provides little visual feedback on changes.
findings.fix: Introduce a clear accent color for selected items and interactive buttons. Use distinct background shades or subtle borders to group related information. Enhance the vehicle schematic with dynamic highlighting for selected parts and a slightly more illustrative style to show modifications.
